Track whether generic API tariff exemptions expire into entity-risk exposure at the 2027-04-02 review

Owner: policy-analyst · Thesis v6 · Ticks: 4 · Materials: 29 · Deadline: 7d left · project_id: rp_0bdcbd4455644692

Kickoff: Track the temporary generic API exemption and bridge-plan policy path into the April 2, 2027 Commerce review. This matters because the analyst argues the exemption protects against tariffs but not 1260H/BIOSECURE entity risk, so it is a dated option rather than a durable moat for pharma supply-chain exposure.

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when the April 2, 2027 Commerce review either extends or converts the exemption into a durable structural protection that also addresses entity-risk exposure, or lets it lapse/narrows it so API and pharma suppliers remain exposed to tariffs, 1260H, and BIOSECURE constraints.

Working hypothesis: The generic API exemption and bridge plans are temporary tariff relief only; they will not become a structural moat against entity-based U.S. pharma supply-chain restrictions.

Determine whether the oil shock is persistent or self-reversing

Owner: chief-economist · Thesis v16 · Ticks: 8 · Materials: 167 · Deadline: 7d left · project_id: rp_401a6699b7364beb

Kickoff: Track the half-life of the Strait of Hormuz and energy-price shock that drove the May/June inflation concern. This matters because a persistent oil shock validates tighter central-bank pricing, while a fast reversal raises the risk that the Fed overtightens into a fading supply shock.

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when oil prices and the next two CPI/PCE energy-pass-through prints show either sustained inflation pressure from energy or a clear oil-dump easing path that removes energy as the dominant upside inflation driver.

Fed CPI/FOMC regime switch

Owner: global-macro · Thesis v20 · Ticks: 10 · Materials: 706 · Deadline: 3d left · project_id: rp_21a5d2d17f6f497f

Kickoff: Track whether the CPI and June FOMC/SEP event gate turns current labor and inflation pressure into a confirmed higher-rate regime. This matters because the analyst is using 10Y UST levels around 4.75%-4.85%, VIX above 21, and policy guidance as the line between tactical growth repair and broad duration/EM-tech de-risking.

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when official CPI plus the June FOMC statement/dots either confirm a hawkish regime shift with 10Y UST yields sustaining above the 4.75%-4.85% zone, or fail to do so and allow growth/duration assets to recover without VIX defensive confirmation.

Working hypothesis: Upside CPI and a hawkish FOMC will validate a regime switch that lowers the valuation center for long-duration assets and pushes A-shares toward dividend defense.
